column2: On the authority of Abū Muḥammad ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“None of you truly believes until his inclination follows what I have brought.” A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith; we have narrated it in Kitāb al-Ḥujjah with an authentic chain.
“None of you truly believes”: [with] complete faith, whose people Allah has promised entry into Paradise and salvation from the Fire.
Hawāhu (“his inclination”): with the short final alif; what he loves and what his soul inclines to,

“follows what I have brought”: of this pure and complete Sharīʿah, in that his heart and nature incline to it as they incline to the worldly things he loves, to which he is naturally disposed to incline.
Whoever's inclination follows everything the Prophet ﷺ brought is a believer with complete faith.
Whoever is not like this is not a believer [with complete faith].

This hadith draws on the saying of the Exalted: “But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves…” [al-Nisāʾ 4:65], to the end of the verse.
The obligation to love the Prophet ﷺ and to follow him in what he commands and refrain from what he forbids, without hesitation or faltering.
